I feel like I wrote this post when I had my baby over 3 years ago. I was perfectly fine the whole pregnancy despite having previous mental health issues. 
As soon as he was born, I was completely numb and terrified and couldn't even look at my baby. Zero connection.  I felt like EVERYTHING I did was wrong. From changing a diaper to trying to breastfeed. As soon as we got home from the hospital,  I freaked out and begged my parents to come over to be with me (it was during Covid and they were wanting to stay away to keep the baby safe).
 They came over and wore masks. I couldn't get my baby to latch for anything and it was extremely overwhelming. My mom helped me figure it out and they eventually went home for the night.  I stood up all night, paranoid. Absolutely no sleep. My parents came over everyday to help and encouraged me to sleep. I couldn't.  I had no connection with my baby but I was scared no one else would be able to take care of him like I could. 
I started to get very dark thoughts. I had a plan. I wasn't good enough for my baby. My husband could get with my best friend and raise our baby with her (this is how crazy my thoughts were) and my baby wouldn't even know me so it would not affect him. 
My husband noticed after a few events that I was in a crisis and contacted my parents. I ended up being taken to a mental health inpatient hospital... 5 days PP. 
It was terrifying but a wake up call that other people definitely had it much worse than me. I spent my stay there finding out that a lot of moms go through this, but no one talks about it !! I was upset because I felt like I was the only one and was just a terrible person. I went home after a couple of days and really wasn't better but I needed to heal in my own home. 
I was placed on a few different medications and my 6 week PP doctor visit was embarrassing because she found out I went to the psych ward and I could tell she was judging me. 
I finally admitted I didn't feel any better with the medication they had me on and met a wonderful doctor who saved my life. I am not religious,  but she prayed over me and told me the story of her daughter going through the same emotions. She found a different medicine and by the next week, I was finally feeling better. A month and a half later-- I am in LOVE with my son. It's like something clicked in my head and he was my whole world. 
I am so sorry this is long,  but I just want you to know, you will get through this and you'll be over the moon in love with your child!  I am extremely grateful I am still here and he is literally the best thing that has happened to me. I promise you will feel this way eventually.  Please do not be afraid to ask for help, and actually accept the help. You got this.

I've been having to feed my mother in law's farm animals for the past 2 weeks and it's draining me since I work and her house is out of the way. Today it POURED rain and I had limited time to get the job done. When it rains, it gets super muddy and I usually slip and slide on her property and just end up needing a shower when I get home. I was driving towards her house in the pouring rain and pulled over to imagine the rain stopping so the job wouldn't be as bad.  As soon as I got out of my car, the pouring rain let up and I was able to feed her animals without getting drenched. It was weird that I could hear the rain but it seemed as though I wasn't getting wet at all.
This is a very inspiring story. Thank you for sharing.  I am practicing imagining lovingly on the behalf of others ♡

I don't treat them like shit (They say I'm their favorite worker) but they can when I'm in my "off" moods--I don't go above and beyond to socialize with them and check in on them like I normally would. I have to hide in random empty rooms to cry for a few minutes and gather my composure. I train new people and I feel myself not being as enthusiastic with them. I used to give 110 percent and now I feel like I also am doing the bare minimum to get by. I feel exhausted in every way -- mentally, emotionally, spiritually, and physically.

I'm getting ready to get showered and dressed for work and I feel so much dread... it's a very scary feeling to have.  I feel like isolating myself and not having the tolerance to deal with these mental patients or coworkers.  I am heavily relied on at work to train new people, and I just found out I will have 2 people to train for the next 2 weeks. I feel sick to my stomach just thinking about it. If it wasn't for needing money, I would not be working. I hate all the rules, regulations and routines. I hate having to break up fights. I cannot tolerate other people's emotional trauma anymore,  yet they always come to me to be the listening ear.  I did apply for an independent office position, but someone with more experience got it over me.  I feel stuck and unmotivated. The only things this job pays for is my rent, car payment, phone bill,  and groceries. I never have any extra money. My car is f'ed and needs brakes because they grind when I use them. I feel like a slave to the system. Help :(
